title: Eastman and Laird Commentary on TMNT #8 — David Choe cohosts
summary: Ed Piskor and Jim Rugg host Kevin Eastman, Peter Laird and David Choe for a page-by-page discussion of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #8, the 1986 Cerebus crossover with Dave Sim. The episode is unusually strong on physical comics production: treatments, collaborative layouts, dialogue polish, photocopy preservation, mailed pages, Sim's redrawing/inking/lettering, Duoshade, Zip-A-Tone, airbrush, frisket, balloon planning and original-page division. Eastman and Laird distinguish their creator-owned black-and-white comic from the child-facing animated adaptation, describing both retained approval and flexibility. Choe's central reading is that friendship, brotherhood, visible fun and serious commitment to a ridiculous premise made the work resonate; he explicitly labels imagined parts of that collaboration as fantasy, and the creators partly confirm the chemistry while acknowledging later difficult periods. The panel traces Richard Corben, Barry Windsor-Smith, Jack Kirby, George Romero, Tom Savini, Time Bandits and other influences; examines the black-and-white boom, parody books and fan letters; and closes with current creator promotion plus a long Cartoonist Kayfabe house ad. Sales, royalty, ownership, credit, contract and market-collapse numbers remain attributed memories pending primary records. Choe's speculation, sexualized Renet commentary and mental-illness metaphor remain uncensored but are not upgraded into biography, diagnosis or neutral metadata. Five public participants are known at episode level, but automatic captions contain zero publisher speaker prefixes, so named line-level turns remain withheld.

source_notes.assessment: No. Preserve the oral-history influence while withholding private identity and relationship reconstruction.

source_notes.assessment: Choe explicitly says he is making that up; Eastman offers a narrower memory about influence and sales resentment. Keep those evidence levels separate.
